answer: Bind each identity to the radio fingerprint of one device: flaws in a Wi-Fi chip distort its signal the way a raven's call belongs to one bird, filed at sign-up. A second identity needs a second radio, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real chips at $25 each. The fingerprint is re-checked each epoch, and a mismatch, or one fingerprint shared across keys, burns a 100 POA bond locked for 12 epochs. Limits: a canyon of RF noise blurs readings, so borderline matches go to human review, and a stolen device can be re-registered, so liveness checks plus slashing keep the gate honest, hard as a walnut shell.
